resolutions.reason: The mark under tav is a single horizontal stroke (patah). It is not sheva+dagesh or tsere. Yod appears to carry vertical dots (sheva). I can't confirm a dagesh in nun at this size, so none is transcribed.
Under the first mem there is a horizontal stroke with dots beside it (hataf-patah), not a bare two-dot sheva. The second mem has hiriq.
The first glyph is rounded with no projecting base stroke at bottom right. Compare the bet of the next word בְּגִלְעָד, which has a clear foot. Kept as kaf whatever the English says.
Under alef there is a flat horizontal stroke with no descending stem (patah).
The first vav has its dot at mid-height beside the stem (shuruk). Nothing sits over the head.
Vertical two-dot sheva under tav. Patah under kaf. I can't see a dagesh in kaf, so none is transcribed.
Under alef a qamats has dots beside it (hataf-qamats). It is wider than the plain qamats under tav.
Qamats under shin and a vertical two-dot sheva under qof. No dagesh in qof.
The mark under zayin has a descending stem (qamats). The patah under alef in the same word is flat, which makes a useful comparison.
The dot sits over the left (sin) arm.

A pale grey partial impression stands in the yod position right after the patah-dalet, followed by a wider than normal space before אֵין. It is weak inking, not a missing letter. Keep the yod. Record the faintness as a physical print defect, not a sic.
Two dots under yod (sheva). Three diagonal dots under nun (qubbutz), not a qamats. Patah under ayin.
The dot is over the vav head (holam). A single dot under tav (hiriq).
The tiny role mark has three letter forms. Earlier role marks on s270 lines 11/16/21 and s272 line 14 are two-glyph ח׳.
